documents.unit: University of Houston System, Information Security
documents.title: Usage of Artificial Intelligence at UHS
documents.stance_why: The page is security and privacy guidance and says "UHS is developing an official AI policy." It lets AI tools be used "freely" on public information, bans only Level 1 and 2 data in unapproved tools, and for "Academic use of AI tools" tells readers to "check with the provost’s office at your System university." It sets no academic stance, so it hands the decision on.
documents.summary: System-level IT security guidance on safe AI use: which data may not enter unapproved tools, accuracy and privacy cautions, and controls for AI agents and self-hosted models. It says nothing about student work and sends academic questions to each university provost. An official policy is stated to be in development.

units.why: The System states it is "committed to ensuring that all constituents can use AI tools" safely and responsibly, which sets an institution-level purpose and principle for AI use; P56 fits better than P02 because it welcomes use only within a safe-use frame.
units.anchor: committed to ensuring that all constituents can use AI tools

units.why: "this security and privacy guidance may evolve" as circumstances change or further policy is developed is an explicit statement that the guidance is provisional, so it is a revisit-the-policy statement (P54).
units.anchor: this security and privacy guidance may evolve as circumstances change
units.frag_end: further policy regarding the use of AI

units.why: "UHS is developing an official AI policy" and until then the guidelines apply: it states the policy process and interim status. P84 is nearest (how the policy is being made); it does not give a body or date, hence the fit note.
units.anchor: UHS is developing an official AI policy
units.fit_note: Says an official policy is still in development and these guidelines apply in the interim; no process, body or date is named.

units.why: "Do not use confidential, sensitive, or mission critical data (Level 1 data) ... with unapproved AI tools" is a prohibition on data entered into AI, which is a data-protection rule (P50), not a ban on use of AI for coursework.
units.anchor: Do not use confidential, sensitive, or mission critical data (Level 1 data)

units.why: "You may use AI tools freely when using non-university or public information" is a permissive default for low-risk data. P02 is nearest; it is not a general default for coursework, so a fit note is added.
units.anchor: You may use AI tools freely when using non-university or public information
units.frag_start: You may use AI tools freely
units.frag_end: through the use of the tools
units.fit_note: The freedom applies only to public or non-university information or newly created content, as a data-risk rule, not a general academic stance.

units.why: "Sharing information with AI applications such as ChatGPT could cause data to be used by the tool for future use" explains the data risk behind the guidance, so it is a privacy statement (P50) that informs.
units.anchor: could cause data to be used by the tool for future use

units.why: "it is critical that you verify any answers an AI tool ... provides" because models "hallucinate" or give biased information: students and staff must check AI output, which is P31.
units.anchor: it is critical that you verify any answers an AI tool
units.frag_end: contemporary context to questions they answer

units.why: "Be mindful that any information you make available ... could be used for AI training" advises users to think about what data they share; it is a data-privacy caution (P50) phrased as advice.
units.anchor: Be mindful that any information you make available to others

units.why: "Please check with the provost’s office at your System university regarding specific use cases of AI tools in your curriculum" hands curricular AI rules to each member university, which is P85 (units set their own rules); the System itself sets no academic stance.
units.anchor: check with the provost’s office at your System university
units.fit_note: Sends users to each System university provost for curricular AI use instead of letting schools set rules; it does not authorize or describe such rules.

units.why: "improving your AI literacy through online training such as courses on Linkedin Learning" recommends training to users, which is P70 (AI-literacy training), as a tip and not a requirement.
units.anchor: improving your AI literacy through online training

units.why: "If you would like advanced Copilot features, contact your IT department for a Copilot Pro licenses" points to licensed tools through IT; P92 (use university-licensed tools) is nearest, but it is an optional paid upgrade.
units.anchor: contact your IT department for a Copilot Pro licenses
units.frag_start: If you would like advanced Copilot
units.fit_note: Describes how to obtain a paid Copilot Pro license through IT rather than telling users to use approved tools.

units.why: "UHS faculty/staff can use Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat with their UHS M365 account" names a sanctioned, university-provided tool for faculty and staff, so P92 over P17 (P17 is course-specific).
units.anchor: UHS faculty/staff can use

units.why: "Review your OneDrive/Sharepoint files to ensure that you are not oversharing" tells Copilot users to check file access, a data-protection step (P50) written as a directive.
units.anchor: Review your OneDrive/Sharepoint files to ensure that you are not oversharing

units.why: The sentence defining AI agents as "autonomous or semiautonomous software entities" sets what the agent guidelines cover, so it is a definition of scope (P61).
units.anchor: autonomous or semiautonomous software entities that utilize AI techniques
units.frag_start: AI agents as autonomous or semiautonomous
units.frag_end: in their digital or physical environments.

units.why: "Agents must use unique, non-human identities (service accounts) with dedicated credentials" is a security requirement for deployed agents; no type covers identity and access control for agents, so it is UNCOVERED rather than stretched to P07 (which is about student editor rules).
units.anchor: Agents must use unique, non-human identities (service accounts) with dedicated credentials
units.uncovered_note: Technical security rule on identity and access management (unique service accounts, least privilege, read-only default) for deployed AI agents.

units.why: "Enforce least privilege across systems, data, and tools" is part of the same agent access-control group, a security rule with no matching type, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Enforce least privilege across systems, data, and tools
units.uncovered_note: Least-privilege access control for AI agents.

units.why: "Require human-in-the-loop approval for high-risk actions" and graduated autonomy limit what agents may do alone. P73 is about decisions on people, so this is UNCOVERED: human approval of risky agent actions.
units.anchor: Require human-in-the-loop approval for high-risk actions
units.uncovered_note: Agents operate within a defined scope, with graduated autonomy by risk level and human approval for high-risk actions.

units.why: "Allow only approved tools for agent use" and the instruction to review third-party skills before enablement is a tool-approval rule, matching P65 (review and approve AI tools).
units.anchor: Review all third-party skills and extensions prior to enablement.

units.why: "all agent behavior must align with university acceptable use policies" requires AI agents to follow existing university policy, which is P77.
units.anchor: all agent behavior must align with university

units.why: "Evaluate all integrations with external agents, APIs, and data sources" and ensuring data sharing meets contractual and regulatory requirements is a review of third-party AI integrations and data sharing, P65.
units.anchor: Evaluate all integrations with external agents, APIs, and data sources

units.why: "Log all agent prompts, data access, and actions performed" and monitoring for anomalies set up documentation and monitoring of deployed AI systems, P98.
units.anchor: Log all agent prompts, data access, and actions performed

units.why: "Regularly review agent usage and business necessity" and decommissioning unneeded agents is periodic review of deployed AI systems, P98.
units.anchor: Regularly review agent usage and business necessity

units.why: The tip that faculty and staff "can explore using Microsoft Copilot Agents to help them become more productive" encourages staff use of a sanctioned tool, with enterprise data protection; P92 fits better than P59 because no teaching task is named.
units.anchor: can explore using Microsoft Copilot Agents to help them become more productive

units.why: For hosting your own LLM, "Work with your local IT department or ISO, and review any implementation with UHS Information Security" requires institutional review before deploying a model, P65.
units.anchor: review any implementation with UHS Information Security

units.why: Checking checksums and avoiding models on the "TX DIR Prohibited Technology & Covered Applications list (i.e. Deepseek)" bans specified AI tools; P65 is nearest (approval of tools) but this is a state-prohibited list, so a fit note.
units.anchor: not prohibited via the TX DIR Prohibited Technology & Covered Applications list
units.fit_note: Names a state list of prohibited AI technologies (e.g. Deepseek) and model integrity checks, rather than a review process.

units.why: "Decide if real data has to be used or if synthetic data would be sufficient" advises minimizing real data in models, a data-protection rule (P50).
units.anchor: Decide if real data has to be used or if synthetic data would be sufficient

units.why: "reset it back to the foundational model as residual training data may remain" is a technical security rule on reusing a hosted model; no type covers it, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: reset it back to the foundational model
units.uncovered_note: When reusing a self-hosted model for a new purpose, reset it to the foundational model because residual training data may remain.

units.why: "If you are unsure whether you are using an AI application safely, please feel free to reach out" invites users to ask security staff first; P10 is nearest (ask when unsure), but the question is about safety, not permission.
units.anchor: If you are unsure whether you are using an AI application safely
units.fit_note: Invites contact with the Information Security Office about safe use, not permission from an instructor.

notes: Single thin System-level IT security page; no academic-integrity or teaching AI rules. Coder B.
